results.title: 2026 Quality Rating System Measure Technical Specifications
results.content: In accordance with the requirements specified in the annual Quality Rating System and Qualified Health Plan Enrollee Experience Survey: Technical Guidance , QHP issuers that offered coverage through a Health Insurance Exchange (Exchange) in the prior year are required to submit third-party validated QRS clinical measure data and QHP Enrollee Survey response data to CMS as a condition of certification. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publishes guidance for Qualified Health Plans (QHP) in the Exchanges to specify requirements for participating in the Quality Rating System (QRS), including the clinical and survey measures that must be reported. HEDIS for QRS measures do not define benefits at the service or metal level (e.g., if the organization offers a pharmacy benefit but does not cover a specific medication class, the member has a pharmacy benefit and is included in the applicable measures requiring this benefit; similarly, if the member has partial coverage of mental health services (either by service or by diagnosis), they are included as having a mental health benefit).

results.title: Data Cleaning (Chapter 21) - The Cambridge Handbook of Research Methods and Statistics for the Social and Behavioral Sciences
results.content: High-quality data are necessary for drawing valid research conclusions, yet errors can occur during data collection and processing. To achieve high data quality, one must approach data collection and management anticipating the errors that can occur and establishing procedures to address errors. This chapter presents best practices for data cleaning to minimize errors during data collection and to identify and address errors in the resulting data sets. Data cleaning begins during the early stages of study design, when data quality procedures are set in place. During data collection, the focus is on preventing errors. When entering, managing, and analyzing data, it is important to be vigilant in identifying and reconciling errors. With these steps, we can ensure the validity, reliability, and representative nature of the results of our research. # Save book to Kindle. results.title: Evaluating Data Quality: Comparative Insights on Standards, Methodologies, and Modern Software Tools
results.content: *   [Regulatory Frameworks for Data Quality](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3038#sec3-electronics-14-03038). *   [Data Quality Assessment Methods](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3038#sec4-electronics-14-03038). The analysis focuses on the following four core areas: (i) types of data and associated quality issues; (ii) quality dimensions and formal standards such as the Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability (FAIR) principles and International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC) 25000 [[16](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3038#B16-electronics-14-03038)]; (iii) research-based methods for data quality assessment; and (iv) contemporary software solutions supporting data quality management. Essentially, quality dimensions offer quantifiable characteristics for evaluating and controlling the quality of data and information [[23](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3038#B23-electronics-14-03038)]. A significant policy framework that establishes thorough standards for data quality management among member states is the European Guidelines 2021 [[35](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3038#B35-electronics-14-03038)]. Comprehensive data quality models are established by ISO 25000, process maturity benchmarks are provided by ISO 15504/CMMI frameworks [[49](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3038#B49-electronics-14-03038)], and software verification and validation are governed by ISO 12207/IEEE 1028 standards [[50](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3038#B50-electronics-14-03038)].
